item.title: Part of RCB's title-winning squad, former India batter announces retirement from cricket
item.description: India top-order batter S Meghana announced her retirement from all forms of cricket on Friday at the age of 30. The Andhra Pradesh cricketer last represented India in October 2022 and played in the Women's Premier League (WPL) for Gujarat Giants and Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB). Meghana announced her decision in a post on Instagram, thanking the game for the experiences and relationships she had built during her career. She also said she intended to remain connected to cricket and work towards helping the next generation of players. "As I announce my retirement from all formats of cricket as a player, my heart is overflowing with gratitude," Meghana wrote in an Instagram post. "The field has been my second home, teaching me resilience, humility, and giving me memories and friendships that I will carry for a lifetime," she wrote. "While my cricket days come to an end, my bond with cricket will never break. I will always stay deeply connected to the game and intend to dedicate my life to giving back to the sport, mentoring the next generation, and serving the game that gave me everything," she added. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Meghana Sabbineni (@meghanasabbineni22) Meghana made her T20I debut against the West Indies in Vijayawada in November 2016, scoring 17 off 16 balls in a 31-run defeat. She made her ODI debut against New Zealand in Queenstown in February 2022, scoring four off 14 balls. She found her rhythm in the next two matches of that series, scoring 49 off 50 balls and 61 off 41 balls. However, those three matches remained her only ODI appearances, in which she scored a total of 114 runs. In 17 T20Is, Meghana scored 258 runs at a strike rate of 102.78, including one half-century. She scored a half-century in both the ODI and T20I formats during her international career. Meghana also played three seasons of the WPL, beginning with Gujarat Giants before joining RCB, where she spent two years. She was part of the Bengaluru franchise's title-winning squad in 2024. Her last appearance in the league came during the 2025 season.

item.title: Fantasy Football Injury Impact: Bijan Robinson's Upside Skyrockets With Brian Robinson Jr Being Ruled OUT
item.description: Atlanta Falcons running back Brian Robinson (15) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Atlanta Falcons have ruled out running back Brian Robinson Jr for Week 7 due to a hamstring injury. We usually don't report on backup running backs, and quite frankly, not many people really care about Robinson Jr. However, people really care about Bijan Robinson, and this is a major development when it comes to Bijan. Falcons injury report: RB Brian Robinson among four ruled out vs. 49ers https://t.co/AvxYadvg9Z pic.twitter.com/TgqJaHbYKG - Around The NFL (@AroundTheNFL) October 23, 2026 Fantasy Impact RB Bijan Robinson, Atlanta Falcons It's Bijan Robinson to the moon this week. This is essentially the equivalent of Jahmyr Gibbs taking over the Detroit Lions backfield without David Montgomery, and we've seen how that goes. Bijan should now see all the volume he can handle without Robinson Jr there to steal his touchdowns. The Falcons play the San Francisco 49ers this week, who are a middle-of-the-pack matchup, allowing the 16th most fantasy points to running backs this season. With this development, Robinson inches much closer to the RB1 overall spot on the week. Nevertheless, we still rank Gibbs as our RB1 because he has a much better matchup against the Green Bay Packers. RB Brian Robinson Jr, Atlanta Falcons Robinson's injury flew under the radar a bit. Probably because we don't see a ton of reports on backup running backs. This is a big one, though. Not only does Robinson Jr hold back Bijan, but he also holds some standalone flex value of his own. We do not know how long Robinson Jr will be sidelined, but Bijan is going to be a fantasy monster for as long as he is out. RB Khalil Herbert, Atlanta Falcons There hasn't been a single running back who has played an offensive snap this season for the Falcons other than Brian and Bijan Robinson. There isn't even another running back listed on their unofficial depth chart. We wouldn't expect any of their other options to see many touches this week, but Bijan also isn't going to play every single snap. We are projecting Herbert to be the next man up, but it could also be Trey Sermon or Jam Miller in the mix. If Robinson is set to miss an extended period of time, we should find out this week who Bijan's handcuff is. item.title: Sabres’ Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen reacts to Connor Hellebuyck trade to Devils
item.description: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images Sabres’ Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen reacts to Connor Hellebuyck trade to Devils appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Buffalo Sabres were linked to a potential Connor Hellebuyck trade for months, leaving Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen to deal with speculation about his own future — but the star goaltender is headed elsewhere. With Hellebuyck joining the New Jersey Devils in a blockbuster on Friday, Luukkonen is welcoming the chance for some of that noise to finally quiet down in Western New York. “It’s going to quiet a lot of conversation around the league. I mean that’s part of sports and that’s what makes sports great is that there’s always those conversations and names thrown around, but I think there’s just so much talk about it. Around the league, around our team,” Luukkonen told The Athletic’s Matthew Fairburn shortly after the deal broke. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I think it’s good for everybody that some of that noise quiets down. But in the end, it’s always gonna be there, especially when you’re at the top level of sports. You’re going to have to learn to deal with it. But in the end, I think it’s a good thing for everybody.” It was widely speculated that Luukkonen would be one of the pieces headed the other way if Buffalo completed a deal for Hellebuyck. General manager Jarmo Kekalainen publicly backed Luukkonen earlier this week , appearing on WGR 550 in Buffalo and saying “we believe in our goaltending,” while calling the Finnish netminder “a big part of our future.” Still, it hasn’t been smooth sailing between the pipes in 2026-27. Luukkonen has a 3.53 goals-against average and .864 save percentage in eight appearances, while Colten Ellis has a 3.19 GAA and .864 save percentage. Alex Lyon, who went on a couple of strong runs last season, is still working his way back from an injury. The Sabres simply need better goaltending if they hope to make last year’s return to the Stanley Cup Playoffs more than a one-off. Currently 4-4-2 after Wednesday night’s 3-1 loss to the Philadelphia Flyers, Buffalo is in last place in the Atlantic Division through 10 games. The Sabres will look to right the ship — likely with Luukkonen between the pipes — against the Washington Capitals in the nation’s capital on Saturday, the start of a four-game road trip. item.title: Dani Olmo happy at Barcelona as January move to Bayern Munich is ruled out – report
item.description: Dani Olmo happy at Barcelona as January move to Bayern Munich is ruled out – report According to journalist Florian Plettenberg , Dani Olmo has no intention of leaving Barcelona, with sources close to the midfielder confirming that he is happy at the Catalan club despite reported interest from Bayern Munich . A January departure is currently ruled out, while the Bundesliga champions are also not actively working on a deal for the Spain international. Dani Olmo happy at Barcelona despite Bayern Munich interest Despite speculation linking him with a return to the Bundesliga, Olmo remains committed to his future at Barcelona. People close to the player have confirmed that he is happy with his situation at the club and is not considering an exit at this stage. Bayern Munich have been linked with the midfielder amid reports that the German side were monitoring potential attacking reinforcements. Not going anywhere. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Olmo has been admired by the Bavarian giants ever since his time with RB Leipzig. His technical quality and versatility make him an attractive profile, but reported interest has not translated into concrete transfer activity. The latest information suggests there is currently no deal being pursued by Bayern. There are no active negotiations over a move, and a transfer during the January window is not on the agenda. Barcelona contract runs until 2030 Olmo’s long-term contract provides further stability amid the transfer rumours. The Spain international is tied to Barcelona until 2030, leaving the club in a strong position and removing any immediate contractual pressure to consider a sale. Since returning to Barcelona in 2024, Olmo has been part of Hansi Flick’s plans, offering creativity and flexibility in attacking areas. Under contract until 2030. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images) He can operate centrally as an attacking midfielder or provide options in wider positions or even as a false nine, making him a useful asset for the team. For now, neither a potential January departure nor a move to Bayern Munich appears to be on the cards. Olmo’s stated happiness at Barcelona, combined with his long-term contract, points towards continuity rather than an imminent change of club. Having suffered an injury during the recent game against PSG , in what his 100th game for the club, the 28-year-old Spaniard will be focused on recovering at the earliest possible.

item.title: Fans lose it as Daniel Ricciardo spotted supporting Liam Lawson at Austin live performance
item.description: Motorsport photo Liam Lawson had some familiar faces in the crowd as he took to the stage in Austin on Thursday night. The New Zealander headlined Garage Sessions with Liam Lawson and Friends at part of Esses Bazaar ATX, held at Inn Cahoots on East Sixth Street ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix. Daniel Ricciardo , who Lawson replaced at Racing Bulls in 2024, was there to watch along with current team-mate Arvid Lindblad and former team-mate Isack Hadjar . Lawson performed alongside his brother Marcus and two childhood friends, Thomas and Harrison, in what was his first public performance since he was 11. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team (@visacashapprb) "I am feeling a lot of things. I mean, I'm excited for... It's a cool opportunity to do this with my brother and a couple of friends that I've grown up playing with," the 24-year-old told the media in Austin ahead of the performance. "To be honest, we haven't done this for like 10 years. And obviously, we never really performed, but we grew up playing together when we were very young. So it's a cool opportunity. But no, I'm sh***ing myself, for sure." When asked if there was more pressure for the live performance than for a grand prix, Lawson added: "Oh my God, like 10 times more pressure for this. I would happily get in a Formula 1 car and go into Q3 over doing this." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team (@visacashapprb) Racing Bulls shared a photo of Lawson and Ricciardo at the event, along with several videos from the performance. "Racing Bulls giving the people what they want," one fan commented, while another added: "Australasia loves to see it." "OH MY GOD, I'M TOTALLY CALM AND COLLECTED ABOUT THIS (I’m 110% screaming)," another fan posted. The United States Grand Prix will take place on 25 October at the Circuit of the Americas. item.title: Latest Lamar Jackson injury update bodes well for Ravens-Bengals tilt
item.description: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Latest Lamar Jackson injury update bodes well for Ravens-Bengals tilt appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Uncertainty continues to hover above Lamar Jackson entering a big divisional matchup versus the Cincinnati Bengals , but the Baltimore Ravens superstar quarterback is at least making progress in his recovery from an ankle injury. How gradual is it, though? Following back-to-back limited practices, Jackson was on the field again on Friday. He did not do much jogging or running during the portion that was open to the media, however, according to ESPN’s Jamison Hensley. Although Jackson’s presence is encouraging, his participation obviously does not guarantee an “active” designation for Sunday’s face-off with Cincy. Friday work @Lj_era8 pic.twitter.com/UCext87gm9 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) October 23, 2026 The Ravens have to balance their pursuit of AFC North supremacy with their franchise keystone’s long-term health. Jackson himself wields some influence over the decision and can potentially give the green light. He cannot just will himself back to full mobility, though. Baltimore must decide if it can properly protect the two-time MVP from further injury, otherwise this squad will find itself in survival mode yet again. If he is on the gridiron, fans should be in for a treat. Jackson and Joe Burrow have contested some memorable battles over the years, and the former usually prevails. The Bengals have a new-look defense, however. They rank tied for sixth in the NFL with 17 sacks (in five games), with huge offseason acquisition Dexter Lawrence accounting for three of them. Baltimore’s offensive line better be ready. But will Lamar Jackson be? The Ravens will ideally update his status by day’s end. Tyler Huntley will make his third consecutive start if No. 8 is forced to miss another game. item.title: Discipline of guarding 24 seconds: Scheierman on how Boston Celtics beat Knicks
item.description: It might only be the start of the third season of Baylor Scheierman's NBA career since being picked up by the Boston Celtics with the 30th overall selection of the 2024 NBA Draft, but he has plenty of experience on how to play the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks with a total of 8 regular season tilts with the Knicks plus a 6-game postseason series vs. New York to his name already. And the Nebraska native had some words to that effect ahead of what will be his ninth collision with the Knicks in the regular season after a Celtics practice on Friday (Oct. 23) morning. "It comes down to the discipline of guarding for 24 seconds," he explained via CLNS Media. "They like to push it, and then if it's not there, it really works the box," Scheierman continued. "So I think it comes down to our discipline of staying consistent throughout the possession, and then finishing possessions with rebounds." New York's two biggest stars, Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns, stood out as particular challenges to the Creighton alum. "One, they're tough shot makers," he said. "And then two, they play well off of each other and you have to be disciplined because they're looking for any sort of angle they can get on you. Especially playing downhill playing off two feet shot fakes stuff like that so it's just a lot of discipline." Boston will need all it can find to avoid starting their season in a 0-2 deficit. But if the Celtics clean up the late-game issues that doomed them on Opening Night vs. the Detroit Pistons , they just might have a shot. item.title: Kon Knueppel & Coby White Injury Update: Why The Hornets May Be In Huge Trouble
item.description: Apr 17, 2026; Orlando, Florida, USA; Charlotte Hornets guard Kon Knueppel (7) passes in front of Orlando Magic forward Tristan da Silva (23) during the second quarter during the play-in rounds of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Kia Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik The Charlotte Hornets opened their season with a road win, beating the Brooklyn Nets 110-103. Charlotte heads to Spectrum Center tonight to take on the Atlanta Hawks, but two starters have already been ruled out: Kon Knueppel and Coby White . Previously, the Hornets stated they would re-evaluate during the first week of the regular season. That time is now, and both players are still out. How concerned should Hornets fans be that Knueppel and White are still out due to injury? Oct 11, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Charlotte Hornets guard Coby White (3) reacts during the second quarter against the Milwaukee Bucks at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Kinser-Imagn Images Kon Knueppel’s Injury Is Extremely Impactful — But Not Alarming Both Knueppel and White sustained injuries during training camp and missed every preseason game. Knueppel has a left hamstring strain, and White has a left calf strain. Soft tissue injuries are always a nuisance in any sport, and Charlotte has kept them out of games out of an abundance of caution. The Hornets were able to squeak by with a win to open the season on Wednesday without Knueppel. Grayson Allen poured in 21 points on an extremely efficient 6-for-9 from the field (5-for-8 from three), showcasing his Sixth Man of the Year potential. Brandon Miller , Naz Reid , Moussa Diabate , and Dennis Schroder all scored 17 or more points. Head Coach Charles Lee’s team got it done that night, but can they expect the same performance against a stronger team like the Atlanta Hawks? The Hornets attempted 48 three-pointers against the Nets, accounting for 51.6 percent of all their shots. They only converted 31 percent of those 48 three-pointers, a brutal reminder of how Knueppel’s efficient shooting helps this offense so much. The turnovers were still relatively high at 20, which was one of the biggest Hornets storylines in the preseason. Knueppel’s hamstring strain is not expected to be long-term. Since the Hornets never officially announced the grade of the strain, it should be assumed to be grade 1 (mild), which carries a shorter recovery timeline. Kon Knueppel at today's Hornets shootaround. That left hamstring is looking pretty good. 🔜 pic.twitter.com/Aomc6Nz91O — r/CharlotteHornets (@HornetsReddit) October 21, 2026 The Hornets are taking a cautious approach with their young star. When the franchise views you as a cornerstone in the post- LaMelo Ball era, it is okay to take it slow to begin the year. Knueppel also doesn’t have an extensive injury history. His next chance to play would be Saturday vs. the Miami Heat. Expect Knueppel to return at some point before the October slate ends. Coby White’s Recurring Calf Injury Is Very Concerning

item.title: Analyst’s source has ‘known Arch Manning a long time’ and makes transfer portal prediction for 2027
item.description: July 15, 2025; Atlanta, GA, USA; Texas quarterback Arch Manning listens to a question during SEC Media Days at the College Football Hall of Fame in Atlanta. The Texas Longhorns entered the season with national title expectations, but consecutive losses to the Oklahoma Sooners and Florida Gators have the program’s College Football Playoff chances on thin ice, and quarterback Arch Manning has been at the center of the struggles. In a column for Bleacher Report, Adam Kramer argued that it might be time for Manning and Texas to part ways. “This would be best for Manning; it would also make sense for Texas,” Kramer wrote. “This once-promising football marriage has lost its luster. And there’s no salvaging it now,” Kramer wrote. Kramer isn’t alone, either. NFL draft analyst Todd McShay has also floated the possibility of Arch returning to college and transferring rather than entering the transfer portal. “Arch Manning — Return. Explore a transfer? — There’s still time to turn this season around. I’m more bullish on his NFL future than the social media doom suggests, but another college season currently looks like his best path,” McShay posted on X. It would appear that where there’s smoke, there’s fire. On a recent episode of the Bill Simmons Podcast, The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero revealed what someone who has known Manning for a long time believes next year has in store for the young quarterback. “I texted one person who’s known Arch (Manning) a long time earlier tonight, and I said, ‘Where do you see Arch in 2027?’ And his response was Ole Miss,” Pelissero said. For now, Manning is still the Longhorns quarterback, and his head coach, Steve Sarkisian, has made it clear what he and the program need from the offense’s leader. “I think that somebody texted me today that we lost the ‘Aw Shucks’ kid and we created something else. I don’t know if we lost him,” Sarkisian said. “We created this. We did. All of us. Y’all included. Me. The whole thing, right. Everybody on ESPN, we’ve created this. And so we’ll see what comes out of it. “But he’s edgy right now. And honestly, I appreciate that about him. At some point, he’s gotta fight back,” Sarkisian said. “And the best way for him to fight back is going out and playing really good football with his teammates and enjoy playing football with his teammates. And so I’m looking forward to watching him compete Saturday night.” Ironically, Texas will face Ole Miss in primetime on Saturday night. item.title: Liverpool not helping Andoni Iraola; €60m transfer plan is a mistake
item.description: Liverpool not helping Andoni Iraola; €60m transfer plan is a mistake Liverpool aren't helping Andoni Iraola with their latest transfer plan. The €60m idea is a mistake. Liverpool are building their transfer shortlist for the upcoming windows and there's certainly work to be done. Richard Hughes left Julian Ward with a very imbalanced squad and one with holes all over the place. On top of that, there are upcoming holes - contracts that need sorting or this group will be decimated by inaction. It's a difficult spot for Ward, then, especially as he needs to sign players pretty quickly. One area of concern is midfield. Liverpool have built a group entirely of attacking midfielders and while the opportunity was there in the summer to sign someone different, the Reds instead sold Curtis Jones and signed no one. It was a bizarre move - but we worry Liverpool could double-down on it. The Manu Koné plan TuttoMercatoWeb reports that Liverpool remain in the mix for Manu Koné. The AS Roma star was the subject of interest by many clubs in the summer, and the report claims that Chelsea mad a €60m offer. That offer was rejected and Roma expect a bigger one to arrive from someone in 2027. The Reds and the Blues are the only clubs named as definitely interested in the Frenchman. But we're not sure about this one. Koné is a very good player but not one proven to be truly elite. That wouldn't usually be a problem - you can always develop a player to that level - but he's incredibly close to what Liverpool already have. Our Value Adder model has Koné as very similar going forward as Ryan Gravenberch. In fact, that's the most similar player to him across the top five leagues in attack. This isn't something that helps Iraola. More of the same isn't the order of the day - the problem isn't squad depth or a need for cover. The issue is that Liverpool don't have controlling, defence-first midfielders who can stop counter-attacks and plug gaps. Koné would be more of the same, essentially a swap-out for Gravenberch in games. Liverpool would largely be in the same position they're in right now, which isn't worth €60m.

item.title: ‘Getting a ring before Luka ‘ – NBA Fans excited for Dalton Knecht as he signs two-way contract with New York Knicks
item.description: Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images Former LA Lakers player Dalton Knecht has found a new home as the New York Knicks signed him to a two-way contract just days after the Purple and Gold outfit waived him. The former Tennessee player was the 17th pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. He had a solid rookie season, but after a poor second year and a disappointing preseason, the Lakers decided to waive him from their final roster. However, just days later, Knecht has been picked by the Knicks, who waived Kevin McCullar Jr. to make room for the former Lakers player. McCullar was one of the players on the Knicks roster who was given the ring on opening night. He had impressive performances for the team, but the franchise decided to give Knecht a chance to prove his talent to the rest of the league. In the preseason, Knecht scored 11 points against the Golden State Warriors in one game and went scoreless in two others. His form has been in decline since the Lakers decided to trade him away, and a deal was even in place with the Charlotte Hornets. But after it collapsed due to Mark Williams’ failed medical, Knecht had to return to Los Angeles. After that debacle, he has failed to find himself, which is why a change in environment could prove to be massive for him. Fans react to Dalton Knecht signing with the New York Knicks Knecht had a top rookie season. In a game against the Utah Jazz, he scored 37 points, draining 9 three-pointers, a record for a rookie in the NBA. Despite his performances, the team included him in a trade package for Mark Williams; from then on, he failed to replicate the talent that was on display until February of 2025. There is evidence that Knecht is a tremendous shooter. While it has not been on display in a long time, the Knicks are playing a gamble that can be fruitful. Fans were excited to hear that the team had added another promising talent to the roster. “Dalton getting a ring before Luka,” said one fan. An account named Real App on X added: “Knicks going back-to-back confirmed.” Someone also stated: “Let shooters shoot……. We are wishing the best for this ex Laker.” “This is a good swing for a player with shooting upside. If it works out, Knicks get an elite shooter. If it doesn’t, who cares. Good buy low from the Knicks,” a fan opined. An account user remarked: “Good luck Dalton! Hopefully getting recruited by the champs is the confidence boost he needs.” Knecht has a chance to do something special with the Knicks and even convert his two-way into a standard NBA contract. The team has a lot of special players who are selfless. He will have to adapt to this, as it is the only way he can succeed in the organisation. It’s officially transformed baseball from a game of potential human error into a high-stakes, high-tech game of poker. The numbers tell a fascinating story about who holds the cards, when they bluff, and how October baseball has turned up the volume on digital appeals. During the regular season, according to MLB, the ABS quietly established its rhythm. Teams challenged an average of 4.4 pitches per game, or roughly 2.2 challenges per team, with human eyes proving far from perfect as players walked away with a 53.9% overturn rate. It operates on a secure network developed by Major League Baseball (MLB) with T-Mobile . Most fans love it, as do the players I’ve spoken to about it. It’s officially transformed baseball from a game of potential human error into a high-stakes, high-tech game of poker. The numbers tell a fascinating story about who holds the cards, when they bluff, and how October baseball has turned up the volume on digital appeals. During the regular season, according to MLB, the ABS quietly established its rhythm. Teams challenged an average of 4.4 pitches per game, or roughly 2.2 challenges per team, with human eyes proving far from perfect as players walked away with a 53.9% overturn rate. By the playoffs, the safety net shrank and the stakes skyrocketed. Through the end of the National and American League Championship Series, challenge usage climbed slightly to 4.6 pitches per game, and accuracy surged to a 60.5% overturn rate. When every single pitch can define a season, players stop guessing and start calling out genuine mistakes with surgical precision. But players aren’t challenging the first pitch they dislike. The ABS challenge is a limited resource, and teams covet it like gold. Early on in games, from the 1st through the 3rd innings, players initiated only 28.6% of all challenges as managers and players hoarded their two allotted appeals. By the 7th inning and beyond, those stored challenges came out of the vault to account for 39.1% of all reviews. The raw volume of challenges across different counts can be equally deceiving. The majority of regular-season challenges, 59.6% occurred in 0-0 counts, which sounds high until you realize 0-0 is the most frequent count in baseball. In reality, players challenged a tiny 2% of all 0-0 pitches. The true battles occurred on edge-case counts where a single call alters an entire at-bat. On 3-2 counts, players challenged 9.3% of all pitches, representing the highest challenge rate of any count. More broadly, 6.2% of all three-ball pitches were challenged compared to 4% of two-strike pitches. A missed call on 0-0 is an annoyance, but a missed call on a full count is the difference between a game-changing walk and an inning-ending strikeout. Comparing how tonight’s teams navigated the system reveals starkly different strategies. The Brewers adopted an aggressive, fire-at-will approach. After averaging 2.4 challenges per game in the regular season (8th most in MLB) with a 52.8% overturn rate, Milwaukee ramped up to 3.4 challenges per game in the postseason so far while improving its success rate to 59.2%. The Brewers used the system as an offensive weapon, putting relentless pressure on the opposition. The Rays went in the opposite direction. After averaging 2.1 challenges per game in the regular season (13th in MLB) with a matching 52.8% overturn rate, they dialed back to a disciplined 1.4 challenges per game in the playoffs. Their reward for extreme restraint was a staggering 69% overturn rate. They rarely challenged, but when they did, the robo-ump almost always agreed. Interestingly, during the regular season, catchers initiated 53% of all challenges, batters accounted for 45%, and pitchers managed 2%. Pitchers, watching from 60 feet and 6 inches away through a wall of bodies, simply lack the visual angle to contest borderline pitch locations. Brewers star pitcher Jacob Misiorowski told me this summer that he completely trusts his catcher to challenge, and I feel most pitchers agree. And with good reason: In the postseason, catchers have cemented their status as masters of the strike zone by initiating 61% of all challenges, while batter usage dropped to 39% and pitchers initiated just one challenge. Equipped with a squatted view right behind the glove, modern catchers are no longer just framing pitches but acting as real-time judges, deciding in a fraction of a second whether to trust the umpire’s call or overrule it with a flick of their wrist. ABS has added incredible drama to games. And I expect in the World Series, the timeliness and importance of each call may be crucial to which team will win its first-ever Fall Classic title. item.description: Brazil in Libertadores and Copa Sul-Americana finals for sixth year running Palmeiras and Atlético-MG represent Brazilian football in the CONMEBOL Libertadores and CONMEBOL Sudamericana finals, respectively Credits: Cesar Greco/Palmeiras and Pedro Souza/Atlético For the sixth consecutive year, Brazilian football will have representatives in the finals of the CONMEBOL Libertadores and CONMEBOL Sudamericana, South America's premier club competitions. In the Libertadores final, Palmeiras will face Estudiantes, while Atlético-MG will take on Boca Juniors in the Sudamericana. In the Libertadores, Brazilian dominance is even greater. Since 2019, teams from the country have won every edition. In 2020 (Palmeiras vs. Santos), 2021 (Palmeiras vs. Flamengo), 2022 (Flamengo vs. Athletico-PR), 2024 (Botafogo vs. Atlético-MG) and 2025 (Flamengo vs. Palmeiras), the finals were all-Brazilian affairs. In 2019, Flamengo defeated Argentina's River Plate, and in 2023, Fluminense beat fellow Argentine side Boca Juniors. During this period, Palmeiras won the title in 2020 and 2021. Having also been crowned champions in 1999, they are chasing a fourth title and will face Argentina's Estudiantes, winners in 1968, 1969, 1970 and 2009, who beat Flamengo on penalties this Thursday (22). To reach the final, the Alviverde defeated Fluminense, also on penalties, on Wednesday (21). The CONMEBOL Libertadores final will take place on November 28 at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo, Uruguay. __instagram:https://www.instagram.com/p/De0gh-gDsRT/?cplk=MWVodmJ1ejk1bXlpeg==__ Brazil has had representatives in the CONMEBOL Sudamericana final for six seasons. Over that period, only Athletico-PR, in 2021, lifted the trophy, beating Red Bull Bragantino. Since then, São Paulo (2022), Fortaleza (2023), Cruzeiro (2024) and Atlético-MG themselves (2025) have finished as runners-up. This year, Galo have the chance to win their first title in the competition and bring the Sudamericana trophy back to Brazilian football. In the semifinals, they eliminated Uruguay's Montevideo City Torque on Wednesday (21) and will face Boca Juniors in the final, after the Argentine side knocked out Vasco on Tuesday (20). The final will take place on the 21st of next month at the Estadio Metropolitano Barranquilla in Barranquilla, Colombia. __instagram:https://www.instagram.com/p/DexorB_jtA-/?obrf=MXVqNjZqdXByemZvbQ==__ This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Jaylen Brown Calls Out Ex-Celtics Teammate Jayson Tatum Over Comments on 76ers Trade
item.description: Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum on April 29, 2025 in Boston Credit: Maddie Meyer/Getty NEED TO KNOW Sixers’ Jaylen Brown called out his former teammate Jayson Tatum in a comment on social media Brown posted a “cap” emoji on an interview Tatum did sharing his recount of learning Brown was being traded to Philadelphia in July Tatum said he was “just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world” when the news of Brown’s trade was announced Jaylen Brown called out his former teammate Jayson Tatum ’s recollection of learning the Celtics traded Brown to Philadelphia. In a video shared to his YouTube on Thursday, Oct. 22, Tatum, 28, shared his recount of the moment he learned the Boston Celtics had traded his longtime teammate to the Philadelphia 76ers in July. Tatum said he was in Las Vegas at the time, and recalled ESPN insider Shams Charania breaking the news to him. “I just got done playing pickup the first day. Shams walks over, he hands me the towel, he’s like ‘Yo, put this over your face, don’t react, they just traded him,” Tatum said. Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum on March 20, 2026 Credit: Grant Burke/NBAE via Getty The Celtics star shared that he asked Charania where the Celtics sent Brown, and when he learned it was Philadelphia — where Brown would team up with LeBron James — he recalled thinking they “traded him down the street.” Tatum said he was “just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world” after his teammate was traded, but it appears that Brown doesn’t entirely believe Tatum’s recount. In the comments of a clip of Tatum’s interview, Brown, 29, reacted with an emoji of a baseball cap, which in internet lingo means you’re calling “cap” on someone and accusing them of lying. Brown and Tatum shared the court in Boston for nine seasons. The Celtics finalized their trade with the Sixers on July 6, sending Brown to Philadelphia in exchange for Paul George, a 2028 first-round pick, a 2031 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2030 second-round pick. The duo led the Celtics to the 2024 NBA championship, and Brown was named the Finals MVP. Read the original article on People

item.title: Browns’ Todd Monken reveals bold Deshaun Watson ceiling bet that could push Shedeur Sanders out
item.description: Browns’ Todd Monken reveals bold Deshaun Watson ceiling bet that could push Shedeur Sanders out originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken chose Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders by chasing ceiling, and six games into the 2026 season, the offense looks like that wager. Speaking on Ryan Clark’s podcast “The Pivot,” Monken said his staff measured both quarterbacks by their peak snaps. Sanders produced highlights of his own, he said, “but we just saw a little bit more from Deshaun at the top end.” “I think you try to look at what a player’s best is and then try to minimize the weaknesses,” Monken said. That logic explains both halves of Cleveland’s 4-2 start. Watson has now led four drives that put the Browns ahead late in games, precisely the peak plays Monken was buying. The floor surfaced against Baltimore, when Cleveland gained 46 net yards and punted on five straight possessions before halftime, then edged the Ravens 13-10 to grab first place in the AFC North. Monken settled on Watson on Aug. 24 after weighing offseason workouts, training camp, a joint session with Buffalo and two exhibition games. Sanders finished last season as the starter and went 3-4 in seven games. Watson was coming off two Achilles surgeries, carrying a $230 million guaranteed contract and facing fans still angry over the se*ual as*ault accusations, his league suspension and the draft capital Cleveland spent to land him. Shedeur Sanders’ Trade Market Hinges on the Same Peak-Play Test In Monken’s telling, one of Watson’s biggest moments came before a snap. Ahead of the Week 4 game against Pittsburgh, the Browns introduced him last out of the tunnel, and a crowd that had booed him roared instead. “They want good football. They want our players to play well,” Monken said. Cleveland beat the Steelers 27-24 after a scoring march in the final stretch flipped the lead. Against Baltimore, Watson found Jerry Jeudy for 33 yards on a 10-play, 62-yard possession that ended with Andre Szmyt’s game-winning field goal. Monken pinned the slow starts on himself and his offensive staff while backing his quarterback’s instincts. “But he’s just got something in him, the ability to make a play when needed,” he said. “We’re always under construction.” The ceiling standard also frames what comes next for Sanders. He hired an agent earlier this month, a move widely read as a step toward leaving, with the trade deadline under three weeks away. Yet the evaluation that kept him on the bench is the same one rival front offices would run, and Sanders has had no chance this season to display the progress he made in camp. With little outside demand so far, a deal won’t come easily. Monken’s offense gets its next chance to raise its floor Sunday at Tennessee, where the 1-5 Titans are waiting. item.title: Texas football knows what it expects. Does it know what it needs?
item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 17: Head coach Steve Sarkisian of the Texas Longhorns reacts in the first half against the Florida Gators at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images In January 2013, Mack Brown was still the head coach at Texas, coming off a nine-win season . A regent and a former regent were already on the phone with Nick Saban’s agent . Saban stayed at Alabama. News of his contract extension broke that December, minutes before Brown was scheduled to speak at the Texas football banquet, and Brown stepped down the next day . Three weeks later, Texas hired Charlie Strong , a coach it never really wanted in the first place. Red McCombs, whose name is on the business school, ripped the hire on the radio . Since Brown, Texas has hired a fallback, a cure, and a better version of the cure. Strong, a defensive coach, took over his own defense’s play-calling in his third year and never posted a winning record . So Texas swung the other way with Tom Herman, the offensive coordinator for Ohio State’s 2014 national champions . When Herman hit a wall, Texas hired more or less the same coach again in Steve Sarkisian: Herman with fancier pre-snap motion, scripted play designs, and a better résumé. He has accomplished more at Texas than either predecessor. Texas keeps shopping for the hot name or the offensive mind. The job has always been bigger than either. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images In January 2013, Mack Brown was still the head coach at Texas, coming off a nine-win season . A regent and a former regent were already on the phone with Nick Saban’s agent . Saban stayed at Alabama. News of his contract extension broke that December, minutes before Brown was scheduled to speak at the Texas football banquet, and Brown stepped down the next day . Three weeks later, Texas hired Charlie Strong , a coach it never really wanted in the first place. Red McCombs, whose name is on the business school, ripped the hire on the radio . Since Brown, Texas has hired a fallback, a cure, and a better version of the cure. Strong, a defensive coach, took over his own defense’s play-calling in his third year and never posted a winning record . So Texas swung the other way with Tom Herman, the offensive coordinator for Ohio State’s 2014 national champions . When Herman hit a wall, Texas hired more or less the same coach again in Steve Sarkisian: Herman with fancier pre-snap motion, scripted play designs, and a better résumé. He has accomplished more at Texas than either predecessor. Texas keeps shopping for the hot name or the offensive mind. The job has always been bigger than either. Greg Davis ran his offense for 13 seasons and called the plays, and Brown kept final say over every call . “I hear every play,” Brown said. He knew he was a capable CEO. In the 12 seasons since Brown left, Texas has gotten there four times . The end wasn’t pretty. Texas went 5-7 in 2010 and never won more than nine games again under Brown. Texas still jumped the gun. It went shopping before it knew what it was shopping for, and it hasn’t stopped. Texas is like nowhere else in the country — the coaches, the fans, the expectations, the donors, the money. The athletic director who hired Strong was fired less than two years later , after a plane towed a “Patterson Must Go” banner over the stadium. Herman won his last game at Texas, a bowl blowout, and was fired four days later , three weeks after his athletic director said publicly that Herman was the coach . But only time will tell if that’s the best thing at the end of the day for Texas’ Fight(ing) chances moving forward.

item.title: Lakers vs. Clippers: What to watch in second game of season
item.description: The Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) controls the ball during an NBA basketball game against The Golden State Warriors on October 21st, 2026 at crypto Arena in Los Angeles, California LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Lakers established an early connection around the basket in their season opener. Their next opponent found plenty of success inside, too. After beating the Golden State Warriors 127-105 on Wednesday, the Lakers host the Clippers on Friday at Crypto.com Arena, with both teams looking to build on convincing opening-night victories. Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler combined for 77 points in the Lakers’ win. Now, L.A. could get its first look at another offseason addition as Collin Sexton prepares to join the rotation. Here are three things to watch in the Lakers’ second game of the season. Who wins the battle in the paint? Both teams made scoring inside a significant part of their opening-night wins. The Lakers scored 66 points in the paint against Golden State, with Kessler contributing 26 points and nine rebounds. The Clippers scored 56 paint points in their 121-96 victory over Sacramento. Friday presents an opportunity to see which team can maintain that production while making the other work harder around the basket. For the Lakers, that starts with Dončić and Reaves creating openings through their drives and work with Kessler. His screens and rolls can force defenders to choose between stopping the ball and staying close enough to prevent a finish. Defensively, L.A. must limit penetration without surrendering easy passing opportunities behind the help. Kessler’s presence matters, this is a huge test to see what he can bring inside mucking up any shot attempt, but the guards and wings must also need to keep the Clippers from repeatedly reaching him with an advantage. What does Sexton bring to the second unit? Sexton is available after being removed from the injury report, putting him in position to make his Lakers debut following a right soleus strain. His arrival gives JJ Redick another option to initiate the offense and attack the basket when Dončić or Reaves rests. The first thing to watch is how Sexton balances his own scoring opportunities with getting teammates involved. His speed can help create early offense, but also rust can be a factor in his play with not playing a single minute in the preseason. Jake LaRavia’s questionable status with a right ankle sprain adds another variable as Redick assembles his bench groups. Can the Lakers disrupt Darius Garland? Garland scored 30 points in the Clippers’ season-opening win, making him an immediate focus for the Lakers’ perimeter defense. Containing him begins with the Lakers wings in Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams getting the start next to Dončić, Reaves and Kessler. Thybulle had the assignment on Stephen Curry in the opener, so look for him to take on the Garland assignment for this matchup as well.

item.title: ‘He’ll Probably Never Get Over It’ — 7-Time NBA All-Star Reacts to Jaylen Brown Calling Out Jayson Tatum’s Comment on Celtics-76ers Trade
item.description: ‘He'll Probably Never Get Over It’ — 7-Time NBA All-Star Reacts to Jaylen Brown Calling Out Jayson Tatum’s Comment on Celtics-76ers Trade One of the biggest NBA talking points on Friday morning was Jaylen Brown publicly calling out his former Boston Celtics teammate Jayson Tatum on social media. While fans continue to discuss Brown’s unexpected reaction, former 7-Time NBA All-Star Joe Johnson has offered his thoughts on what might have prompted it. Joe Johnson’s Explanation of the Reason Behind Jaylen Brown’s Comment During a recent episode of the “Nightcap” podcast, Johnson joined Shannon Sharpe and Chad Johnson. At one point, the cast addressed Brown’s decision to publicly question Tatum’s comments about his departure from Boston. Johnson believes Brown is still struggling to accept the trade that sent him to the Philadelphia 76ers. According to the former NBA star, leaving a franchise where he spent so many years and achieved considerable success is not something Brown can easily forget. “It’s tough, bro. When y’all want a title together, y’all been so dominant together and you got to get rid of one guy. That’s tough on Jaylen. That’s tough, bro. Yeah, that’s probably a hurt, JB… He’ll probably never get over it,” Johnson said on the podcast . However, Johnson also believes that the situation could give Brown additional motivation as he looks to move forward with his career in Philadelphia. “But at the same time, he needs that fire in his belly to continue, you know, to continue to be great, you know, throughout his career because he’s gonna wear that on his sleeve, homeboy,” Johnson added. The controversy began after Episode 3 of Tatum’s “Summer of Jayson” video series, titled “The Sit Down,” was uploaded to his YouTube channel. In the episode, Tatum took viewers through his training during the 2026 offseason. He also discussed Brown’s July trade from the Celtics to the 76ers. “We were in Vegas. I just got done playing pick-up the first day. Shams walks over. He hands me the towel, and he’s like, ‘Yo, put this over your face. Don’t react. item.description: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Packers LB Zaire Franklin’s status for Lions bout revealed in latest injury update appeared first on ClutchPoints . Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions after he suffered a shin injury during practice on Thursday. Head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Friday that the veteran defensive captain has been ruled out . Franklin’s absence creates another challenge for Green Bay’s defense, which has already lost starting linebacker Edgerrin Cooper for the season because of an Achilles tendon tear. Cooper suffered the injury in Week 4, leaving the Packers without both of their Week 1 starting linebackers for the trip to Detroit. LaFleur indicated that Franklin is not expected to require injured reserve, which would force him to miss at least four games. However, the team is still assessing the severity of his injury. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 30-year-old has been a key contributor through six games, leading the Packers with 48 tackles and ranking second on the team with 15 stops, according to Pro Football Focus. He has also played 414 defensive snaps this season. With Franklin unavailable, Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper are expected to take on larger responsibilities. McDuffie has started in Cooper’s place over the past two weeks, while Hopper, a 2024 third-round draft pick, could receive an opportunity to play a more regular defensive role. Nick Niemann and veteran special-teamer Kristian Welch are also options for the linebacker rotation. Green Bay will face a big test against the Lions’ running game, led by running back Jahmyr Gibbs. He has recorded 504 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns, ranking fifth in the NFL in rushing yards and tied for second in rushing scores. He has also produced 27 receptions for 243 yards and two receiving touchdowns. Detroit’s offense is averaging 32.8 points per game, tied with the Buffalo Bills for the league lead. The Lions have also exploited McDuffie in the past as quarterback Jared Goff completed all nine passes thrown toward the linebacker in their 2024 meeting, producing 68 yards and a touchdown in the team’s 34-31 win . The timing of his latest injury could hardly be worse for Franklin, as the Packers are scheduled to play on Thursday Night Football in Week 8, potentially extending his absence to a second game. It would be a rare setback for the defender, who had missed only one game throughout his NFL career before the latest setback. item.title: NRL stalwart Starling joins St Helens
item.description: Tom Starling spent eight seasons at Canberra Raiders, scoring 17 tries [Getty Images] St Helens have signed experienced NRL hooker Tom Starling on a three-year contract. Starling is the fourth close-season signing for Saints, who missed the Super League play-offs for the first time after finishing seventh in 2026, following the arrivals of Sean O'Sullivan, Christian Tuipulotu and Solomona Faataape. Starling played under new Saints head coach Kevin Walters when he turned out for the Prime Minister's XIII against Papua New Guinea Prime Minister's XIII. Starling said: "I've seen how intense he is with his training and so when he called and asked if I'd be interested in coming, he spoke about his plans for the club and what he wants to achieve. I was ready to go there and then." Saints chief executive Abi Ekoku said: "Tom's desire to join the club has been infectious and his hunger for success stands out. "Saints supporters will embrace his skill, leadership and fierce competitiveness."

item.title: 49ers Given Clear Option to Trade QB Mac Jones Before Deadline
item.description: Over the last couple of years, the San Francisco 49ers have been connected to quite a few rumors surrounding quarterback Mac Jones. Last season, Jones stepped in for Brock Purdy when the starter went down with injury early in the year. Jones performed admirably, proving that he was still capable of being a starting NFL quarterback. In 11 games played in 2025, the 28-year-old quarterback completed 69.6 percent of his pass attempts for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions. He has yet to throw a pass this season. That has led to more rumors before the upcoming November 10 trade deadline. Jones could simply remain with the 49ers and give the team excellent backup quarterback depth. If something were to happen to Purdy, San Francisco would be able to continue performing at a high level offensively. Should John Lynch and the 49ers’ front office decide to open up to the idea of trading Jones, a few different teams would likely have interest. With that being said, one team in particular has been connected to a possible trade for Jones. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images 49ers Handed Clear-Cut Trade Destination for QB Mac Jones The Athletic has released a big board of 50 potential trade candidates before the 2026 deadline. When it came to Jones, they only suggested on landing spot. That landing spot was none other than the Philadelphia Eagles, who recently ruled Jalen Hurts out for the rest of the season due to blood clot issues. “Jones is one of the best backup quarterbacks in the league. He should, at some point, get another chance to start. That will most likely come in 2027, as Jones is in the final year of a two-year deal he signed with the 49ers,” they wrote. “But could a team in need of a quarterback — like the Eagles, if they don’t take the retool avenue — convince the 49ers to make a deal with an over-the-top offer? It’s unlikely. But again, we’re trying to have fun here. The 49ers are contenders after a 6-0 start, and keeping some insurance behind MVP frontrunner Brock Purdy makes more sense.” After being selected with the No. 15 overall pick by the New England Patriots in the 2021 NFL Draft, Jones struggled to find consistency. He has played in 64 total games, throwing for 12,741 yards, 67 touchdowns, and 50 interceptions. More than likely, the 49ers will simply hold onto Jones through the deadline. But, the Eagles are a team worth monitoring if Lynch decides to consider a move. item.description: Celtic Target January Defensive Midfielder: Has The Summer Planning Failed? Celtic’s domestic form has offered encouragement, but their European campaign has exposed questions about the balance of Martin O’Neill’s squad. The Scottish champions have lost their first three Europa League league-phase fixtures, leaving little room for further mistakes. A 7-1 victory over Hearts displayed Celtic’s attacking threat, yet domestic results cannot disguise the demands of European football. O’Neill needs dependable options across the pitch, particularly when injuries and suspensions disrupt his preferred starting XI. Summer recruitment brought significant changes to the squad. Celtic signed striker Kasper Høgh for a reported £11 million and added winger Haissem Hassan, while several late arrivals expanded their options. However, the departures of Arne Engels, Daizen Maeda and Reo Hatate reduced the squad’s established quality in key areas. Those sales reportedly generated a net transfer surplus of £35.5 million, although Celtic must balance that figure against their recruitment costs and other financial commitments. The late arrivals offered additional depth, but integrating new players takes time, particularly when the manager needs immediate consistency in European competition. Callum McGregor remains central to Celtic’s midfield structure. The captain provides positional discipline and helps the team move possession forward, yet relying heavily on one player creates obvious risks across a demanding season. Mika Baur, Joël van den Berg and Oliver Sørensen provide midfield alternatives, although the squad still needs a specialist defensive presence. According to Celts Are Here , Celtic continue to prioritise a defensive midfielder for January while assessing centre-backs to address defensive absences. Recruitment chief Tam Mullen faces the task of finding players who can contribute immediately rather than requiring months of adaptation. item.title: José Mourinho ready to hand surprise start to Real Madrid star vs Barcelona
item.description: José Mourinho ready to hand surprise start to Real Madrid star vs Barcelona A member of the midfield ranks at La Liga giants Real Madrid has late this week been tipped for what would come as a somewhat surprising start in the club’s upcoming showdown with Barcelona. José Mourinho’s Real squad are of course currently in the thick of preparations for their most important fixture of the season to date. On Sunday evening, Los Blancos will make the trip to the Spotify Camp Nou, to lock horns with arch rivals Barcelona. The latter have had the number of their Clásico opponents over recent seasons, with Real Madrid have emerged triumphant from just one of their last seven meetings with Barca. In the knowledge that another defeat this weekend could dent his side’s La Liga title ambitions beyond repair, José Mourinho is therefore considering springing a surprise on Blaugrana counterpart Hansi Flick. As per a report from Marca , Eduardo Camavinga’s candidacy to feature from the off in Catalunya is ‘gaining momentum’. Frenchman Camavinga has been used sparingly across the season to date, but ‘possesses qualities that the Real Madrid coaching staff considers crucial for trying to contain Barcelona’s attack’. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Mikel Arteta admits 'not good signs' as Arsenal suffer HUGE Bukayo Saka injury blow
item.description: FC Bayern München v Arsenal FC - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal will be without star winger Bukayo Saka for their upcoming Premier League fixture against Everton after he sustained a thigh injury. Manager Mikel Arteta admitted the early signs are concerning, with the player set for an MRI scan to determine the full extent of the issue. Arsenal suffer major Saka injury blow Saka has been officially ruled out of Saturday's Premier League fixture against Everton. The 25-year-old is dealing with a thigh injury and requires further medical assessment before a return timeline can be established. The England international sustained the issue just ten minutes into 2-2 Champions League draw against Bayern Munich . He attempted to continue but was ultimately forced off the pitch due to the problem. Arteta admits concerning signs for winger The precise severity of the injury remains unclear, prompting significant concern for Arsenal. Arteta confirmed that the player is undergoing further evaluation to understand the true extent of the damage. "He's going for an MRI this afternoon because he had a lot of fluid in the area, so it was difficult to understand the severity of the injury. We will know tomorrow," Arteta told a press conference on Friday. "We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists. When a player is struggling to walk off the pitch and he's restricted in his movement, they are not good signs. So again, let’s be a little bit patient so we can give a definitive assessment and then let you know." Arsenal boss frustrated by fixture congestion The timing of the setback has amplified concerns over player welfare at the highest level. Following the injury to his star winger, Arteta took the opportunity to highlight the immense physical strain placed on modern squads. The Arsenal manager actively called for greater consideration from football's governing bodies. He stressed that teams are being pushed to their absolute physical limits. "If they can support the amount we are putting into these players, it would be really appreciated," he said. "We have to play three times in less than six days, the games are so demanding, we are chasing until the last minute." A demanding schedule awaits the squad Arsenal must now navigate their immediate domestic duties without one of their most influential attackers. The club will eagerly await the weekend MRI results to establish whether the winger faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines. The immediate focus shifts to securing three points at home against Everton this Saturday. Arteta will need to shuffle his attacking options to compensate for the significant absence on the right flank. The relentless run of fixtures will not ease up after the league clash. Arsenal are subsequently scheduled to visit fourth-tier Fleetwood Town in the League Cup fourth round on Tuesday.

item.title: Yankees linked to offseason trade for Brewers' 18-HR All-Star
item.description: Yankees linked to offseason trade for Brewers' 18-HR All-Star originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees may be very busy this offseason. After falling short in the postseason, general manager Brian Cashman will be looking at potential roster upgrades. One position of need is at catcher. Austin Wells is a strong defender behind the plate but leaves much to be desired hitting-wise. New York should be looking for a right-handed platoon partner for Wells in free agency, or they could make a big splash via trade. Bleacher Report's Zach Buckley believes the Milwaukee Brewers could look to trade William Contreras this offseason, despite the club's run to the World Series. "Trading Contreras wouldn't help the Brewers now (or maybe any time soon), but it might be what's best for the franchise's future. "If they aren't prepared to pay what it'll cost to keep him next offseason, then moving him during this one could be the best option on the board," Buckley wrote. Buckley predicts the Yankees will acquire Contreras, who is one year away from free agency, from the Brewers this winter. MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player Contreras, a three-time All-Star, is one of the best hitting catchers in baseball. He hit .270/.341/.417 with 18 home runs and a .758 OPS in 147 regular season games. That offensive production would be a huge upgrade over Wells, who hit .186/.292/.332 with 14 homers and a .624 OPS. The Yankees would probably have to send Milwaukee one Major League-ready pitcher and a few prospects to secure the trade for Contreras, but it might be worth it to help balance their lineup. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...
